A human should decide whether EndCountryOrArea/EndLocation should also move to the Mexican interconnect or stay at Presidio, TX as the intentional US-side commercial endpoint; either way the row should acknowledge the pipe itself crosses the border. validity.researcher_notes: Trans-Pecos Pipeline's Presidio border-crossing facility is part of the SAME FERC-certificated project as the mainline, not a separate pipeline: FERC's Presidential Permit for the 'Presidio Crossing' authorizes 1,093 feet of 42-inch pipe on the US side (HDD from a meter facility on the north side of the Rio Grande) plus 907 feet of 42-inch pipe on the Mexican side, from the international boundary to a point in Mexico, where it interconnects with the Ojinaga-El Encino Gas Pipeline near Manuel Ojinaga, Chihuahua (naturalgasintel.com, 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline Border-Crossing Facility Gets FERC Thumbs-Up'). EIA's own Wahalajara System writeup (todayinenergy, id=44278) independently describes Trans-Pecos as one of the US border-crossing pipelines feeding this same Ojinaga interconnect into Mexico's grid. The flagged route's Mexico-side endpoint (29.668, -104.538) sits about 20 km northwest of Presidio -- consistent with the drawn line continuing past the ~300 m HDD crossing itself to the actual physical interconnect/meter point inside Mexico, not with a boundary-precision artifact (those are meters, not multiple km). So the geometry is corroborated as a genuine cross-border facility. This is a sheet-classification question (CountriesOrAreas/EndCountryOrArea), not a geometry fix, so no coordinates are proposed -- per standing rule 8, geometry review stays with a human/the routes repo if the exact vertex placement needs refining.
